title: Встреча с Нагиевым и визит Елены  (Meeting Nagiyev and Elena's Visit)

segments.t: Out in the dining room, Nagiyev warmly welcomes Chef Barinov back from the hospital and jokes about his health. Barinov makes Nagiyev promise not to tell Elena Pavlovna that he skipped his vacation, right as Elena herself walks into Claude Monet with friends.
Как новенький ты был в начале века.
Не выдавай меня, я тебе потом объясню.
Виктория Сергеевна, может быть, я сама?
Alright, let's go through it step by step in English.
'Let me call you right back.' In Russian, the idea of 'give' flows naturally into 'will call back' without extra filler words.
'Glad to see you.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'glad' before landing on 'to see'.
'Thank you for the kind words.' Sasha brings out the contrast between 'thank you' and 'on' in a few short words. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'I am kidding, just kidding.' The meaning hinges on 'am joking' working together with 'am joking' in spoken Russian.
'How are you feeling?' Vika anchors the line on 'how', while 'yourself' completes the thought.
'Oh, stop saying that.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'come on' and finishing on 'drop it'. Chef Viktor answers right away.
Как новенький ты был в начале века.
'The last time you were good as new was at the turn of the century.' Notice how Russian expresses 'how' and 'centuries' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
'There is just so much work to do.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'of work' before landing on 'much'.
Не выдавай меня, я тебе потом объясню.
'Do not give me away, I will explain everything to you later.' The grammar packs 'not' and 'I will explain' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'I am not at the restaurant right now.' In Russian, the idea of 'by' flows naturally into 'there is no' without extra filler words.
'A head chef fresh from Paris.' Vika brings out the contrast between 'head chef' and 'only' in a few short words.
Виктория Сергеевна, может быть, я сама?
'Viktoriya Sergeyevna, maybe I should take that table myself?' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'Viktoriya' and finishing on 'myself'. Chef Viktor answers right away.

'There are only three people sitting there.' Notice how Russian expresses 'there' and 'a person' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Alright, let's listen to all those lines again from the top.
Как новенький ты был в начале века.
Не выдавай меня, я тебе потом объясню.
Виктория Сергеевна, может быть, я сама?
